title: Model source cryptographic audit and tamper-flagging workflow
creator: Aisha R. Patel
summary: Add a cryptographic checksum and signature-based audit stage to the model onboarding pipeline that flags tamper indicators and ties into temporary pin/quarantine flows before performance profile publication.
description:
Motivation: Several recent onboarding runs surfaced models with mismatched artifacts (weights uploaded separately from manifests) and ambiguous licensing metadata. We need an automated cryptographic audit that verifies checksums/signatures of model artifacts, detects tampering or post-hoc mutation, and produces a tamper flag that gates subsequent steps (version pinning, profile publication, release).

Scope: implement a pipeline stage in the onboarding flow that consumes the model package (manifest, weights, tokenizer, config), computes canonical checksums (sha256) for each artifact, verifies any attached signatures (pgp/ed25519), and records a tamper_result: {"clean"|"modified"|"missing-signature"}. If tamper_result != clean, the onboarding run should: (1) automatically quarantine the model bundle for manual review, (2) mark the model as "temporary-pin: true" to prevent auto-promotion, and (3) surface an exception ticket for legal/compliance.

Non-goals: not building a full key management system here — we will rely on KMS-backed verification endpoints owned by Security. Also not doing binary-level provenance attestation beyond checksums/signatures in this ticket (future work).

Success criteria: system reduces silent artifact mismatch incidents, and prevents performance profile publication for flagged models until resolution.

Notes: we must ensure the checksum algorithm and canonicalization rules are documented, and that the output is reversible and human-auditable (signed audit-record).
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding pipeline includes a cryptographic audit stage that computes sha256 checksums for manifest, weights, tokenizer, and config files.
If uploaded signatures are present, pipeline invokes signature verification and records verification status.
Tamper decision outcomes: clean, modified, missing-signature, mismatch-manifest are produced and stored in onboarding metadata.
Models with tamper_result != clean are automatically quarantined and marked temporary-pin: true; profile publishing is blocked until status is cleared.
UI/Console shows tamper status on model details page and exposes a one-click 'create compliance review' flow that opens a GitHub issue template populated with audit metadata.
Unit and integration tests cover canonicalization rules and edge cases (partial uploads, zipped artifacts, reordered manifests).
tasks: Design canonicalization rules for model packages (who owns edge cases): Design doc in Confluence.
Implement checksum and signature verification library (runtime team helper) and expose as onboarding REST endpoint.
Add tamper_result field to onboarding metadata schema and propagate to Console and API responses.
Quarantine flow: implement temporary-pin flag and quarantine storage path; trigger notification to Legal/Compliance channel.
Block performance profile publication when temporary-pin is true; unit test the guard.
Console UX: add tamper status badge, details view, and one-click compliance ticket with audit payload.
E2E test: simulate weight mismatch, missing signature, and clean upload scenarios.
decisions: Use sha256 for canonical checksums to align with infra tooling and SRE expectations (low collision risk, widely supported).
Accept both detached signatures (PGP/Ed25519) and embedded signed manifests; if no signature present, mark missing-signature rather than failing onboarding.
Temporary pin semantics: temporary-pin is a soft block that prevents auto-promotion and profile publication but allows manual override after compliance review.
Store signed audit-record in object store (immutable) with a signed envelope rather than trying to re-sign artifacts in-place.
risks: False positives from canonicalization differences (zip ordering, metadata timestamps) could increase manual reviews and slow onboarding.
If KMS verification endpoint has availability issues, onboarding latency could spike — need circuit-breaker and cached verification results.
Legal may require different handling for certain restricted licenses; ensure a clear escalation path and SLA for reviews.
